Claude Code.description: Anthropic's agentic coding tool for Claude models, available as a terminal CLI, IDE extensions, a desktop app and on the web.

Codex.description: OpenAI's coding agent, offered as an open-source terminal CLI plus IDE extension, desktop app and cloud agent, used with OpenAI models via ChatGPT plans or API.

Pi.description: Minimal, extensible open-source terminal coding agent (pi / pi-mono) by Mario Zechner, with a small toolset, TypeScript extensions and support for many model providers; now hosted under Earendil Works.

OpenCode.description: Open-source, provider-agnostic coding agent with a terminal UI plus desktop and web clients; also sells the OpenCode Go/Zen model subscriptions. Made by Anomaly (formerly SST).

Hermes Agent.description: Open-source, self-improving general-purpose AI agent from Nous Research that builds skills and memory from use, runs from the terminal or messaging gateways, and works with many model providers.

Chat UI (web/app).description: Bucket for using general chat interfaces (ChatGPT, Claude Desktop/web, Gemini app, voice modes, self-hosted UIs like Open WebUI) rather than a coding agent.

Custom harness.description: Bucket for self-built or homegrown agent harnesses that commenters wrote themselves.

Cursor.description: Proprietary AI code editor (VS Code fork) with built-in agents, plus a Cursor CLI and cloud agents, sold by subscription by Anysphere.

GitHub Copilot.description: GitHub's AI coding assistant, available as IDE extensions, the Copilot CLI and a cloud coding agent, with access to models from several labs via subscription.

Antigravity.description: Google's agent-first IDE/development platform (often abbreviated AGY) built around Gemini models, with an agent manager for running multiple agents.

Grok.description: xAI's Grok assistant and SuperGrok subscription; also covers xAI's Grok Build terminal coding agent bundled with Grok plans.

Zed.description: Open-source, high-performance code editor written in Rust by Zed Industries, with built-in AI agent panel and support for external agents via the Agent Client Protocol (ACP).

Orca.description: Open-source desktop app (with CLI and mobile companion) for running a fleet of coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex in parallel terminals, each in its own git worktree. Made by Stably AI.

T3 Code.description: Open-source 'agent harness control surface' from T3 Tools (Theo Browne) - desktop (Electron), web and mobile apps that drive locally installed agents like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode and Antigravity.

DeepSeek Harness.description: DeepSeek's open-source (MIT) coding agent harness 'dsh', where every component is a plugin; runs as a CLI, web UI or headless and is used mainly with DeepSeek models. Released August 2026.

Emacs (gptel etc.).description: Bucket for using Emacs as the AI/agent environment, via packages such as gptel (LLM client) and Editor Code Assistant (ECA, eca.dev).

Paseo.description: Open-source, self-hosted daemon plus desktop, mobile, web and CLI clients for orchestrating multiple coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi and others) with worktrees and diff review.

Cline.description: Open-source autonomous coding agent, mainly used as a VS Code extension, also available as a CLI and SDK; bring-your-own model.

Kiro.description: Amazon/AWS's agentic IDE and CLI centred on spec-driven development.

Kilo Code.description: Open-source agentic coding extension for VS Code and JetBrains IDEs (plus CLI) from Kilo, with access to many models.

Goose.description: Open-source, extensible AI agent with desktop app and CLI that works with any LLM; originally created by Block, now under the aaif-goose organization.

Aider.description: Open-source AI pair-programming tool for the terminal that edits code in a git repo using many model providers.

Gemini CLI.description: Google's open-source terminal coding agent for Gemini models.

VS Code.description: Microsoft's open-source code editor, used here as the host for AI agents (Copilot, Claude Code, Cline etc.) and extensions. The source (Code-OSS) is MIT-licensed; the VS Code build Microsoft ships is proprietary.

Maki.description: Open-source (MIT) Rust terminal coding agent by Tony Solomonik focused on low context usage (tree-sitter index, sandboxed code execution), extendable with Lua plugins; supports many providers and ACP.

Devin.description: Cognition's autonomous AI software engineer, used through a web app (with IDE/desktop and Slack integrations).

Kimi Code.description: Moonshot AI's open-source terminal coding agent (Kimi Code CLI, successor to Kimi CLI) for Kimi models.

Muse Code.description: Meta's terminal coding agent powered by its Muse Spark models, launched August 2026 with plans from $5/month.

3code.description: Open-source single-binary command-line coding agent by Carlo Capocasa, focused on token economy (chunked mode, goal files) and built-in sandboxing.

Amp.description: Agentic coding tool from Amp (spun out of Sourcegraph), available as a CLI and editor extension, with cloud runners.

CodeBuddy.description: Tencent's AI coding assistant, offered as an IDE, editor plugins and CLI with free and Pro tiers and access to multiple models.

Mistral Vibe.description: Mistral AI's minimal open-source terminal coding agent for Mistral (and other) models.

JetBrains Thinkrail.description: JetBrains incubator project: an open-source agentic IDE (desktop and mobile) built as a thin layer around the pi coding agent, with per-chat git worktrees and SPEC.md-based project memory.

OpenChamber.description: Open-source fan-made desktop, web/PWA and VS Code interface for the OpenCode agent.

NodeCode.description: Open-source self-modifying agent written in Common Lisp (SBCL) that runs as one long-lived process with a single 'evaluate Lisp' tool.

DeepSeek Superagent.description: DeepSeek's open-source research prototype of an autonomous Router/Worker 'super-agent' built on DeepSeek Harness that responds to and fixes issues in a repository; published October 2026.

JetBrains AI / Junie.description: JetBrains' AI Assistant and Junie coding agent integrated into JetBrains IDEs.

Warp.description: Agentic development environment built around a modern terminal, with built-in agents, from Warp.

Open WebUI.description: Open-source, self-hostable web chat interface for Ollama and OpenAI-compatible APIs, extensible with plugins.

CLI harness (unspecified).description: Bucket for unspecified terminal coding agents (vendor CLIs) without a named product.

Juggler.description: Open-source desktop/browser workbench for AI coding agents by Julian Storer (creator of JUCE), with tree-structured persistent sessions and a headless server for remote machines; vendor-neutral.

ZeroStack.description: Lightweight open-source coding agent written in Rust by gi-dellav, optimized for low memory use, with multiple providers, prompt modes, worktrees and ACP support.

Pendant.description: Unidentified; mentioned once as something a commenter was trying alongside Pi via Paseo, likely an agent client/harness.

Hax.description: Minimalist open-source (MIT) terminal-native coding agent written in C by Oleksandr Chekhovskyi.

FreeBuff.description: Free, ad-supported terminal coding agent from the Codebuff team (YC F24) using open models.

MetaGPT.description: Open-source multi-agent framework that simulates a software company of LLM roles; from FoundationAgents/DeepWisdom.

Dirge.description: Minimal open-source Rust coding agent inspired by pi, opencode and maki, with role-based multi-provider routing, persistent memory and safeguards for cheaper models.

OpenHands.description: Open-source AI software-development agent platform (formerly OpenDevin) with CLI, local GUI and cloud versions.

ZCode.description: Z.ai (Zhipu AI)'s desktop coding-agent app for its GLM models, used with the GLM Coding Plan.

jotter (MCP).description: A commenter's own small MCP server for handing off briefs between AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Codex); not a public product.

Lynx.description: Product at lynx.railcode.dev that a commenter uses in place of agent CLIs; the site gives no details, so its exact nature is unverified.

Ori.description: OpenRouter's family of agent tools: Ori Code, a native terminal coding agent, and Ori Harness, which runs existing agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) through OpenRouter models.

llm-desktop-electron.description: Small open-source Electron app by mkornreich for running a Claude Desktop-style chat UI with non-Claude models (e.g. via OpenRouter).

Corgi.description: Open-source terminal multiplexer/agent manager built on Ghostty and inspired by herdr, for running Claude Code, Codex, Pi and OpenCode sessions.

Grok CLI.description: Terminal coding agent for xAI's Grok models; most likely xAI's official Grok Build CLI (an unofficial open-source grok-cli by superagent-ai also exists).

Kepler.description: GitKraken's agentic development environment that turns issues from trackers (Jira, Linear, GitHub etc.) into tasks run by ACP agents in worktrees, with a Kanban view.

MiMo Code.description: Xiaomi's open-source terminal coding agent (an OpenCode fork tuned for MiMo models), released June 2026.

Swival.description: Small open-source (MIT) Python CLI coding agent aimed at open and local models, with memory, review loops, MCP and A2A support.

Volt.description: Open-source (MIT) fork of the Pi coding agent by Jordan Hans: a terminal coding agent with planning, code review, subagents, Pi-compatible extensions and an iOS companion.

Lyre.description: Lyre Studio's AI workspace for running coding agents across your own computers, with live app previews on phones; builds on Paseo's open-source code.
